_note: Experimental data transcribed from the tabulated NASA reports (not digitized from figures). Numbers are exactly as printed in the reports. Each dataset carries a _source citing report, table/heading and page. Companion to experiments.json (hand-digitized), whose key names are reused where the same quantity exists.

kussoy_fin15._source: Settles, G. S. and Dodson, L. J., 'Hypersonic Shock/Boundary-Layer Interaction Database: New and Corrected Data', NASA CR-177638, 1994; file KUSSOY3.DAT (data of Kussoy & Horstman, NASA TM-103838, 1991, plus supplementary data), report pp. 25-28 = PDF pp. 29-32
kussoy_fin15._file_header: KUSSOY3.DAT -- DATA FILES FROM NASA TM 103838 AND SUPPLEMENTARY DATA SUPPLIED BY THE EXPERIMENTERS ON A SINGLE-FIN, SWEPT SHOCK WAVE/TURBULENT BOUNDARY-LAYER INTERACTION AT MACH 8.2
kussoy_fin15._note_coordinates: Coordinate definitions. The only explicit statement in the data file is the banner 'S = DISTANCE ALONG FIN SURFACE MEASURED FROM LEADING EDGE'. The plate tables are headed 'Z(cm)' (or 'z(cm)') with no further definition; the fin tables are headed 'Y(cm)'. The CR-177638 text (report p. 25) says: 'Fins of 5, 7.5, 10, 12.5, and 15 degree angle-of-attack were mounted on the flat plate. The fin leading-edge position was 176 cm aft of the plate leading-edge. The x,y,z coordinate frame used to describe the measurements is indicated in the sketch below.' In that sketch the origin is at the fin leading edge on the plate, X is drawn along the fin root (parallel to the fin surface, i.e. rotated by the fin angle alpha from the freestream), Y is normal to the plate (up the fin), and Z is in the plate plane normal to the fin surface, pointing away from the fin. Hence Z = 0 is the fin surface and Z increases away from the fin (consistent with the data: the plate streamline angle equals the fin angle at the smallest Z and goes to 0 at large Z, and the peak plate pressure is at Z ~ 0). Z is NOT measured from the plate centerline. Whether the plate 'X' stations (18.19, 16.45, 15.5 cm) are along the fin or along the freestream is not stated in the file; the file uses the distinct symbol S for fin-surface stations (fin pressure at S = 18.34 cm, fin heat transfer at S = 16.70 and 19.62 cm). The previous hand-digitized file (from Edwards & Chandra AIAA 94-2275) labelled the fin stations as X = 17.72 = 18.34*cos(15 deg) and X = 16.13 = 16.70*cos(15 deg), i.e. it treated S as along the fin and X as the freestream direction; those key names are retained here for compatibility but the raw S values are what the file prints.
kussoy_fin15._note_structure: Top-level keys plate_p_X18.2, plate_q_X16.45, plate_cf_X15.5, fin_p_X17.72, fin_q_X16.13 keep the names of the old hand-digitized file and hold the 15 deg fin data. '_additional' sets are the file's 'Additional ...' (redundant/repeat) tables at the same station. Other fin angles are under other_fin_angles.

wideman_flare._source: Wideman, J. K., Brown, J. L., Miles, J. B., and Ozcan, O., 'Surface Documentation of a 3-D Supersonic, Shock-Wave/Boundary-Layer Interaction', NASA TM-108824, 1994, Tables 1-37 (report pp. 58-84 = PDF pp. 64-90)
wideman_flare._note_x_origin: TM-108824 Sec. 2.2 (report p. 3): 'The coordinate system with respect to the model is shown in figure 1. The x-phi-r coordinate system is a cylindrical system aligned with respect to the cylinder centerline axis with x = 0 cm located at the leading edge of the offset flare. The coordinate y coincided with the r coordinate but was measured from the model surface. The coordinate z was in the transverse direction.' Also: 'The cylinder-flare junction along phi = 180 deg was located 6.98 cm downstream of phi = 0 deg. The streamwise locations of the cylinder-flare junction for various azimuths are given in table 2.' and (Sec. 1.2) 'The axis of this conical flare was offset 1.27 cm from the cylinder centerline'. So x is streamwise along the cylinder axis, x = 0 at the most-upstream point of the junction (phi = 0, x_j = 0), and phi = 0 is the azimuth where the flare starts first.
wideman_flare._note_phi: phi = 0 is the side where the flare starts first (x_j = 0, longest afterbody 12.06 cm); phi = 180 is where the junction is furthest downstream (x_j = 6.98 cm, afterbody 5.08 cm). Flare ramp length 11.14 cm along both phi = 0 and 180 (Sec. 2.2). Tables 11-23 were taken with the phi = 0 plane on top of the cylinder; Tables 29/31/35 ('side of cylinder') with the stated azimuth aligned with the side of the cylinder (where LISF was possible), see Sec. 4.5.3.
wideman_flare._note_P_over_Pinf: P_over_Pinf arrays are computed here as (P/Pt) / 0.0332. The report (Sec. 4.4, report p. 32) states: 'The runs were conducted at a total pressure of Pt = 172.37 +/- 0.4% kPa. The average value of Pinf/Pt as measured by the most upstream cylinder tap was 0.0332 +/- 0.6% indicating a free-stream Mach number of Minf = 2.87.' ... 'Along a length of 6.5 cm, the drop in the undisturbed pressure with respect to the most upstream value was 2.2% which amounts to an increase in Mach number of 0.3% to Minf = 2.89.' The factor 0.0332 is the one the report itself uses: Table 26 Ppk/Pinf = (Ppk/Pt)/0.0332 (e.g. 0.0871/0.0332 = 2.62). The nominal Table 1 value Pinf/Pt = 5.54/172.37 = 0.032140 (isentropic value for M = 2.89 is 0.03213) would give P/Pinf about 3.3% higher everywhere (undisturbed taps would read ~1.04 instead of ~1.0). To use the Table 1 factor instead: P_over_Pinf * 0.0332 / 0.032140.
